hook.convey: two same-size wholes, one cut into 4 equal parts, the other into 8 → 8 is the bigger number, yet each of its parts is smaller → which single part to pick is the question

use.hi: Socho, do ek jaise cake hain. Ek cake 4 barabar tukdon mein kata hai, doosra 8 barabar tukdon mein. Tumhe kisi ek cake se sirf ek tukda lena hai.
use.en: Picture two identical cakes. One cake is cut into 4 equal pieces, the other into 8 equal pieces. You take just one piece from one cake.

use.hi: Do ek jaisi drawing sheet hain. Ek sheet 4 barabar hisson mein bati hai, doosri 8 barabar hisson mein. Tumhe kisi ek sheet ka sirf ek hissa colour karna hai.
use.en: Two identical drawing sheets. One sheet is divided into 4 equal parts, the other into 8 equal parts. You colour just one part of one sheet.

explain.convey: one bar = one whole; 4 equal parts; 1 shaded part = 1/4; bottom number = how many equal parts the whole is cut into → predict: more cuts of the same bar, one part smaller

point.hi: Yeh ek poori patti hai. Iske 4 barabar hisse hain, aur ek hissa rang wala hai, woh 1/4 hai. Neeche wala 4 batata hai ki poori patti kitne barabar hisson mein kati hai.
point.en: This is one whole bar. It has 4 equal parts, and one part is shaded; that is 1/4. The bottom number 4 tells how many equal parts the whole bar is cut into.

prompt.hi: Isi patti ko 8 barabar hisson mein kaatein, toh ek hissa pehle se bada hoga ya chhota?
prompt.en: If we cut this same bar into 8 equal parts, will one part be bigger or smaller than before?

explain.convey: same-size bar now in 8 equal parts → each earlier part split in 2 → 1 shaded part = 1/8 → set against the 1/4 part

point.hi: Ab wahi patti dekho. Iske 8 barabar hisse hain, aur ek hissa rang wala hai, woh 1/8 hai. Pehle wala har hissa ab aadha-aadha bant gaya hai.
point.en: Now look at the same bar. It has 8 equal parts, and one part is shaded; that is 1/8. Each earlier part is now cut in half.

prompt.hi: Toh ek hissa kaunsa bada hai, 1/4 ya 1/8?
prompt.en: So which single part is bigger, 1/4 or 1/8?

explain.convey: both on one 0-to-1 line: 1/8 nearer 0, 1/4 further on → 1/8 < 1/4; same whole, more equal parts → each part smaller → bigger bottom number, smaller unit fraction

point.hi: Yeh sankhya rekha 0 se 1 tak hai, aur is par 2 nishaan hain. 1/8 zero ke paas hai, aur 1/4 usse aage. Toh 1/8 < 1/4. Ek hi poore ke jitne zyada barabar hisse, har hissa utna chhota.
point.en: This number line goes from 0 to 1, with 2 marks on it. 1/8 is close to zero, and 1/4 is further on. So 1/8 < 1/4. The more equal parts one whole has, the smaller each part.

prompt.hi: Do ek jaise cake hain. Ek cake ka 1/3 tukda, doosre ka 1/7 tukda. Kaunsa tukda bada hai, 1/3 ya 1/7?
prompt.en: There are two identical cakes: a 1/3 piece of one, a 1/7 piece of the other. Which piece is bigger, 1/3 or 1/7?

problem.hi: Do ek jaise chocolate bar hain. Aman ko ek bar ka 1/6 milta hai, Zoya ko doosre bar ka 1/3. Kise bada tukda milta hai?
problem.en: There are two identical chocolate bars. Aman gets 1/6 of one bar, Zoya gets 1/3 of the other. Who gets the bigger piece?

do.hi: Dono bhinnon ka upar ka number 1 hai, matlab dono ko ek-ek tukda milta hai. Toh sirf tukde ka size dekhna hai.
do.en: Both top numbers are 1, so each gets one piece. We only compare the size of one piece.

why.hi: Ginti barabar hai, isliye size hi faisla karega.
why.en: The count is the same, so size decides.

do.hi: Aman ka bar 6 barabar hisson mein kata hai.
do.en: Aman's bar is cut into 6 equal parts.

why.hi: Neeche ka 6 batata hai ki bar kitne barabar hisson mein kata hai.
why.en: The bottom number 6 tells how many equal parts the bar is cut into.

do.hi: Zoya ka bar 3 barabar hisson mein kata hai. Hisse kam hain, toh har hissa lamba hai.
do.en: Zoya's bar is cut into 3 equal parts. Fewer parts, so each part is longer.

why.hi: Ek hi size ka bar kam hisson mein bante, toh har hissa bada hota hai.
why.en: When a bar of the same size is cut into fewer parts, each part is bigger.

do.hi: Zoya ke har 1/3 ko 2 barabar hisson mein kaato. Ab uska bar bhi 6 hisson mein hai.
do.en: Cut each of Zoya's thirds into 2 equal parts. Now her bar is also in 6 parts.

why.hi: Ek 1/3 ke andar do 1/6 aate hain.

prompt.hi: Aman ke paas 1/6 hai, Zoya ke paas 2/6 jitna. Toh bada tukda kise mila, Aman ko ya Zoya ko?
prompt.en: Aman has 1/6, Zoya has as much as 2/6. So who got the bigger piece, Aman or Zoya?

answer.hi: Zoya ko bada tukda mila, kyunki 1/3 > 1/6.
answer.en: Zoya got the bigger piece, because 1/3 > 1/6.

why.hi: Ek hi size ke bar ko jitne zyada hisson mein kaato, har hissa utna chhota. 1/6 toh 1/3 ka aadha hai, isliye 6 bada number hote hue bhi 1/6 chhota tukda hai.
why.en: The more parts a bar of the same size is cut into, the smaller each part. 1/6 is half of 1/3, so even though 6 is the bigger number, 1/6 is the smaller piece.

prompt.hi: Do ek jaisi roti hain. Ek 10 barabar tukdon mein kati hai, doosri 5 barabar tukdon mein. Kaunsa ek tukda bada hai, 1/10 ya 1/5?
prompt.en: Two identical rotis: one is cut into 10 equal pieces, the other into 5 equal pieces. Which single piece is bigger, 1/10 or 1/5?

accept: the piece from the roti cut into 5

prompt.hi: Ek hi poore ke yeh teen bhinn chhote se bade ke kram mein lagao: 1/3, 1/12, 1/6.
prompt.en: Put these three fractions of the same whole in order from smallest to biggest: 1/3, 1/12, 1/6.

prompt.hi: Yeh sankhya rekha 0 se 1 tak 4 barabar hisson mein bati hai. 0 ke baad pehla nishaan, jahan ? laga hai, 1/8 se bada hai ya chhota?

predict before cutting: 3 vs 6 pieces of one laddoo → rule used without a picture

remediation.move: two same-size strips, one in 4 equal parts, one in 8; two 1/8 parts cover exactly one 1/4 part → a 1/8 part = half of a 1/4 part → more cuts of the same whole, smaller part; 8 > 4 but 1/8 < 1/4

say.hi: Yeh patti 8 barabar hisson mein kati hai, aur 2 hisse rang wale hain. Yeh do 1/8 milkar theek ek 1/4 jitne lambe hain. Matlab ek 1/8 hissa, 1/4 ka aadha hai. 8 bada number hai, par 1/8 chhota hissa hai.
say.en: This bar is cut into 8 equal parts, and 2 parts are shaded. These two 1/8 parts together are exactly as long as one 1/4. So one 1/8 part is half of 1/4. 8 is the bigger number, but 1/8 is the smaller part.

prompt.hi: Asha aur Ravi ke paas ek jaisi juice ki bottle hai. Asha apni bottle ka 1/5 juice nikalti hai, Ravi apni bottle ka 1/10. Kisne zyada juice nikala, Asha ne ya Ravi ne?
prompt.en: Asha and Ravi have identical juice bottles. Asha pours out 1/5 of her bottle, Ravi pours out 1/10 of his. Who poured out more juice, Asha or Ravi?

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab tak har baar ek hi tukda tha, toh tukde ka size faisla karta tha. Ab dekhenge ki neeche ka number same ho, tab kaise tulna karte hain.
bridgeToNext.en: So far it was always one piece, so the piece size decided. Next we see how to compare when the bottom number is the same.

hook.convey: two same-size wholes, each cut into 7 equal parts; one person takes 3 parts of one, another takes 5 parts of the other → same-size parts, so who has more is settled by the top number alone

use.hi: Do ek jaise cake hain, dono 7 barabar tukdon mein kate hain. Riya apne cake ke 3 tukde khaati hai, Sohan apne cake ke 5 tukde.
use.en: Two identical cakes, both cut into 7 equal pieces. Riya eats 3 pieces of her cake, Sohan eats 5 pieces of his.

use.hi: Do ek jaise garden hain, dono 7 barabar kyariyon mein bante hain. Meera apne garden ki 3 kyariyon mein flower lagati hai, Arjun apne garden ki 5 kyariyon mein.
use.en: Two identical gardens, each divided into 7 equal beds. Meera plants flowers in 3 beds of her garden, Arjun in 5 beds of his.

explain.convey: bar in 7 equal parts → each part 1/7; 3 shaded = 3/7 = three 1/7 parts; top number = how many of those equal parts are taken

point.hi: Yeh patti 7 barabar hisson mein kati hai, toh har hissa 1/7 hai. Isme 3 hisse rang wale hain, yeh 3/7 hai. Upar wala 3 batata hai ki aise kitne hisse liye gaye.
point.en: This bar is cut into 7 equal parts, so each part is 1/7. 3 parts are shaded; that is 3/7. The top number 3 tells how many such parts are taken.

prompt.hi: Isi patti ke 5 hisse rang dein, toh woh kaunsa bhinn hoga?

explain.convey: same bar, same 1/7 parts; 5 shaded = 5/7 → part size unchanged, only the count changes → the 'both are sevenths, so equal' belief tested

point.hi: Wahi patti, wahi 1/7 wale hisse. Ab 5 hisse rang wale hain, yeh 5/7 hai. Yahan bhi hisson ka size same hai, bas rang wale hisse zyada hain.
point.en: The same bar, the same 1/7 parts. Now 5 parts are shaded; that is 5/7. The parts are the same size; only more of them are shaded.

prompt.hi: Rohan kehta hai ki 3/7 aur 5/7 barabar hain, kyunki dono sevenths hain. Kya woh sahi hai, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: Rohan says 3/7 and 5/7 are equal because both are sevenths. Is he right, yes or no?

explain.convey: one 0-to-1 line in sevenths: 3/7 = 3 parts from 0, 5/7 = 5 parts from 0 → further from 0 = bigger; same bottom number → compare top numbers

point.hi: Yeh sankhya rekha 0 se 1 tak sevenths mein bati hai, aur is par 2 nishaan hain, 3/7 aur 5/7. 5/7 zero se zyada door hai. Jab neeche ka number same ho, toh upar ka number dekho. Jo zero se zyada door, woh bada.
point.en: This number line from 0 to 1 is cut into sevenths, with 2 marks on it, 3/7 and 5/7. 5/7 is further from zero. With the same bottom number, look at the top number. The one further from zero is bigger.

prompt.hi: Do ek jaisi roti hain. Ek roti ka 2/5 hissa, doosri ka 4/5 hissa. Kismein zyada roti hai, 2/5 ya 4/5?
prompt.en: Two identical rotis: 2/5 of one, 4/5 of the other. Which is more roti, 2/5 or 4/5?

explain.convey: rule holds only with matching bottom numbers → same-size pieces → more pieces = more; bottom numbers differ → piece sizes differ → the count of pieces alone decides nothing

point.hi: Baayein taraf neeche ka number same hai, toh same size ke hisse, aur zyada hisse matlab zyada. Daayein taraf neeche ke number alag hain, toh alag size ke hisse, aur sirf hisse ginne se faisla nahi hota.
point.en: On the left, same bottom number, so same-size pieces, and more pieces = more. On the right, different bottom numbers, so different-size pieces, and pieces alone do not decide.

prompt.hi: Neeche ke number alag hon, jaise 2/3 aur 3/10. Kya tab zyada hisson wala bhinn hamesha bada hota hai, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: When the bottom numbers differ, like 2/3 and 3/10, is the fraction with more pieces always bigger, yes or no?

problem.hi: Do ek jaise cake hain. Meena apne cake ka 5/8 khaati hai, Raju apne cake ka 3/8. Kisne kam cake khaya?
problem.en: There are two identical cakes. Meena eats 5/8 of her cake, Raju eats 3/8 of his. Who ate less cake?

do.hi: Dono bhinnon ka neeche ka number 8 hai, matlab dono cake ke tukde ek hi size ke hain. Har tukda 1/8 hai.
do.en: Both bottom numbers are 8, so the pieces of both cakes are the same size. Each piece is 1/8.

why.hi: Neeche ka number same hai, toh tukdon ka size bhi same hai.
why.en: Same bottom number, so the pieces are the same size.

why.hi: Upar wala 5 batata hai ki Meena ne kitne tukde khaye.
why.en: The top number 5 tells how many pieces Meena ate.

why.hi: Upar wala 3 batata hai ki Raju ne kitne tukde khaye.
why.en: The top number 3 tells how many pieces Raju ate.

prompt.hi: Sab tukde ek jaise hain. Toh kam cake kisne khaya, Meena ne ya Raju ne?
prompt.en: All the pieces are the same size. So who ate less cake, Meena or Raju?

answer.hi: Raju ne kam cake khaya, kyunki 3/8 < 5/8.

why.hi: Neeche ka number same hai, toh tukde same size ke hain. Phir jiske tukde kam, uska cake kam. Sankhya rekha par bhi 3/8, 5/8 se pehle aata hai.
why.en: The bottom number is the same, so the pieces are the same size. Then fewer pieces means less cake. On the number line too, 3/8 comes before 5/8.

prompt.hi: Meena ne ek cake ka 2/6 khaya aur uske bhai ne usi cake ka 4/6. Zyada kisne khaya: Meena ne ya uske bhai ne, ya dono ne barabar?
prompt.en: Meena ate 2/6 of a cake and her brother ate 4/6 of the same cake. Who ate more: Meena or her brother, or did they eat the same?

prompt.hi: Do ek jaise cake hain. Asha ka cake 4 barabar tukdon mein kata hai aur woh 2 tukde leti hai. Ben ka cake 12 barabar tukdon mein kata hai aur woh 3 tukde leta hai. Ben kehta hai ki uske paas zyada hai, kyunki 3 tukde 2 se zyada hain. Zyada cake kiske paas hai, Asha ya Ben?

prompt.hi: Ek hi cake ka 3/4 bada hai ya 5/6? Dono mein poore cake se ek tukda kam hai.

2/9 vs 5/9 asked as the smaller → same rule read the other way

say.hi: Yeh sankhya rekha 0 se 1 tak sixths mein bati hai. Neeche ka 6 sirf hisse ka size batata hai, kitna mila yeh nahi. 2/6 aur 4/6 ke hisse ek hi size ke hain, aur 4/6 mein aise zyada hisse hain. Isliye 4/6 zero se zyada door hai, aur zyada hai.
say.en: This number line from 0 to 1 is cut into sixths. The bottom 6 only tells the size of a part, not how much you have. The parts of 2/6 and 4/6 are the same size, and 4/6 has more of them. So 4/6 is further from zero, and it is more.

remediation.move: both shares on one 0-to-1 line in twelfths: 3/12 = 3 twelfths, 2/4 = 6 twelfths → 2 quarter-pieces reach further than 3 twelfth-pieces → the count of pieces decides only when the pieces are the same size, i.e. same bottom number

say.hi: Dono hisse ek hi sankhya rekha par rakho, jo 12 barabar hisson mein bati hai. 3/12 sirf 3 chhote hisson tak jaata hai. 2/4 toh 6 chhote hisson tak pahunchta hai, kyunki ek 1/4 teen 1/12 ke barabar hai. Hisse tabhi gino jab unka size same ho.
say.en: Put both shares on one number line cut into 12 equal parts. 3/12 reaches only 3 small parts. 2/4 reaches 6 small parts, because one 1/4 equals three 1/12. Count pieces only when they are the same size.

prompt.hi: Do ek jaise bar hain. Ek bar 3 barabar tukdon mein kata hai, usme se 2 tukde lo. Doosra 12 barabar tukdon mein kata hai, usme se 4 tukde lo. Kaun zyada hai, 2/3 ya 4/12?
prompt.en: Two identical bars. One is cut into 3 equal pieces and you take 2. The other is cut into 12 equal pieces and you take 4. Which is more, 2/3 or 4/12?

accept: 2 pieces of the bar cut into 3

remediation.move: one 0-to-1 line in twelfths: 3/4 = 9 twelfths, gap to 1 = 3 twelfths; 5/6 = 10 twelfths, gap to 1 = 2 twelfths → both one piece short, but the missing pieces differ in size → smaller gap = closer to the whole = bigger

say.hi: Is sankhya rekha par 12 barabar hisse hain. 3/4 nau hisson tak jaata hai, 1 tak pahunchne mein 3 hisse baaki hain. 5/6 das hisson tak jaata hai, sirf 2 hisse baaki. Dono mein ek tukda kam hai, par kam wale tukde ka size alag hai. Jiska gap chhota, woh 1 ke zyada paas, aur wahi bada.
say.en: This number line has 12 equal parts. 3/4 goes up to 9 parts, 3 parts short of 1. 5/6 goes up to 10 parts, only 2 parts short. Both are one piece short, but the missing pieces differ in size. The smaller gap is closer to 1, and that one is bigger.

prompt.hi: Do ek jaise bar hain: ek ka 4/5, doosre ka 9/10. Dono mein poore se ek tukda kam hai. Kaunsa bada hai, 4/5 ya 9/10?

draw two same-size strips, 2/3 and 2/6 → picture made by the child, not given
3/4 vs 3/8, says what differs → piece size named, an eighth = half a quarter
5/8 vs 5/12 of metro maps, asks why → explanation, not just the pick
3/4 vs 4/5, both one piece short → size of the missing piece decides, tops differ

remediation.move: two same-length strips laid on one 0-to-1 line: 3 quarter-pieces reach 3/4, 3 eighth-pieces reach only 3/8 → same number of pieces, quarter-pieces longer → 3/4 reaches twice as far

say.hi: Dono patti ek hi sankhya rekha par rakho. 1/8 wale 3 tukde sirf 3/8 tak pahunchte hain. 1/4 wale 3 tukde 3/4 tak jaate hain, jo do guna door hai. Tukde utne hi hain, par 1/4 wale tukde lambe hain.
say.en: Put both strips on one number line. Three 1/8 pieces reach only 3/8. Three 1/4 pieces reach 3/4, which is twice as far. The number of pieces is the same, but the 1/4 pieces are longer.

prompt.hi: Do ek jaise bar hain. Ek ka 4/5 rang wala hai, doosre ka 4/10. Kiska rang zyada lamba hai: 4/5 wale ka ya 4/10 wale ka, ya dono barabar?
prompt.en: Two identical bars: 4/5 of one is shaded, 4/10 of the other. Whose shading is longer: the 4/5 or the 4/10, or are they equal?

remediation.move: two same-size ribbons on one 0-to-1 line in twelfths: a sixth = 2 twelfths → 5/6 = 10 twelfths; 5/12 stops at 5 twelfths → bigger bottom number → smaller pieces → with the same top, 5/12 is shorter

say.hi: Dono ribbon ek hi sankhya rekha par rakho, jo twelfths mein bati hai. Ek 1/6 do 1/12 ke barabar hai, isliye 5/6 utna hi hai jitna 10/12. 5/12 usse kaafi pehle ruk jaata hai. Neeche ka number bada, toh hisse chhote, aur upar ka number same ho toh woh bhinn chhota.
say.en: Put both ribbons on one number line cut into twelfths. One 1/6 equals two 1/12, so 5/6 is as much as 10/12. 5/12 stops well before it. A bigger bottom number means smaller pieces, and with the same top number that fraction is smaller.

prompt.hi: Do ribbon hain, dono 1 m lambe. Ek ka 2/3 kaata, doosre ka 2/6. Kaunsa kata hua tukda lamba hai, 2/3 ya 2/6?
prompt.en: Two ribbons, each 1 m long. 2/3 of one is cut off, 2/6 of the other. Which cut piece is longer, 2/3 or 2/6?

remediation.move: two same-size bars with the missing piece of each named: 4/5 is missing 1/5, a bigger gap; 5/6 is missing 1/6, a smaller gap → compare the size of the missing pieces, not their number → 1/6 < 1/5 → 5/6 is missing less → 5/6 bigger

say.hi: Baayein 4/5 hai, isme 1/5 kam hai, yeh bada gap hai. Daayein 5/6 hai, isme 1/6 kam hai, yeh chhota gap hai. Dono mein ek tukda kam hai, par kam wale tukde ka size dekho. 1/6 chhota hai 1/5 se, toh 5/6 mein kam kami hai, isliye 5/6 bada hai.
say.en: On the left is 4/5, missing 1/5, a bigger gap. On the right is 5/6, missing 1/6, a smaller gap. Both are one piece short, but look at the size of the missing piece. 1/6 is smaller than 1/5, so 5/6 is missing less, so 5/6 is bigger.

prompt.hi: Do ek jaise bar hain: ek ka 2/3, doosre ka 3/4. Dono mein poore se ek tukda kam hai. Kaunsa bada hai, 2/3 ya 3/4?
prompt.en: Two identical bars: 2/3 of one, 3/4 of the other. Each is one piece short of a whole. Which is bigger, 2/3 or 3/4?
